8.A  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC-2023-003; a Resolution of the Planning

  Assistant Planner Sam Dominguez presented this item.

  Chair Nemeth opened the public hearing on this item.

  Justin Robinson, representing the applicant Crown Castle introduced himself and was
  available for any questions.

  Chair Nemeth thanked the applicant for bringing this project up to speed on the timeline.

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing.

  Vice Chair Henderson asked why it has taken 2 to 3 years to obtain the Conditional Use

  Mr. Robinson responded that time delays resulted from Covid and the site as it did not
  meet the current codes.

  the project is Categorically Exempt from environmental review.

  Assistant Planner Sarah Stachnik presented this item.

  Chair Nemeth opened the public hearing on this item.

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing.

  Commissioner Alvarez asked if any applications have been received for development on
  this site.

  Chair Nemeth responded to Commissioner Alvarez’s question and stated that there are
  no plans for development at this site.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-002; a Resolution of the Planning
  Commission of the City of Palmdale, approving Tentative Parcel Map 83805, as
  amended, and find that the project is Categorically Exempt from environmental review.
  Moved by: Vice Chair Henderson and seconded by Commissioner Fraga-Saenz
  Motion passed with five Yes votes.
 8.C  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC-2023-001; a Resolution of the Planning
  Commission of the City of Palmdale, recommending approval of Zoning Ordinance
  Amendment 21-007 and find that the project is consistent with Program Environmental
  Impact Report 22-002 prepared for the City’s General Plan (Palmdale 2045).

  Planning Manager Taggart opened the presentation and explained this is update is a
  replacement of the entire Zoning Code, which is intended to ensure consistency with the
  General Plan to comply with the recently adopted State Laws and create a more user
  friendly modern document.

  Associate Planner Jasmine Almora presented this item with an overview of the staff report
  and made herself available for any questions.

  Chair Nemeth opened the public hearing on this item.

  Mr. Mark McGaughey, Real Estate Broker with CBRE, spoke in opposition to the item
  related to all drive through distance separation requirements.

  Chair Nemeth confirmed that the Commissioners are in receipt of written statements
  submitted by RY Properties, Belldale, LLC, Clearpath Holdings, LLC, and Shaughne S.
  Warnack Trust.

  Mr. Rick Norris, representing Belldale, LLC, and spoke in opposition to the item. He asked
  that staff look at the 500 feet limitations related to the drive through distance separation
  limitations to be reconsidered and modified.

  Greg Quan, RY Properties, spoke in opposition to the item related to the drive through
  distance separation limitations. He stated that he has submitted his concerns in writing.

  Barry Munz, AV Engineering, spoke in opposition to this item related to the distance
  separation limitations.

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing on this item.

  Vice Chair Henderson asked what is being done in other cities related to the drive through
  distance separation requirements.

  Commissioner Alvarez asked if there’s a City that compares to Palmdale that has
  implemented the same type of limitations.

  Associate Planner Almora stated there are other cities that have implemented this
  restriction, but the demographics and climate is different compared to Palmdale.

  Vice Chair Henderson asked that staff consider revisions to these requirements.

  Planning Manager Taggart stated that the intention is not to restrict development, but
  create consistency with the General Plan as it relates to distance separations.

  Commissioner Alvarez asked if the push for these requirements is directed more toward
  safety and from input from the community.
   Planning Manager Taggart responded to Commissioner Alvarez that the safety and
  circulation of traffic is a direct reflection of a policy that has been adopted in the General
  Plan.

  Commissioner Elize commented that he agrees this restriction is directed to safety.

  Vice Chair Nemeth agreed with the alignment of the Zoning Code and the General Plan.
  She stated concerns with the drive through distancing and directed staff to look at this
  particular section and work with developers on this before it goes to Council for approval.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-001, Recommending approval of Zoning
  Ordinance Amendment 21-007, as amended, and find that the project is consistent with
  Program Environmental Impact Report 22-002 prepared for the City’s General Plan
  Palmdale 2045.
  Moved by: Vice Chair Nemeth and seconded by Commissioner Fraga-Saenz
  Motion passed with five Yes votes.

8.D  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC-2023-004; a Resolution of the Planning
  Commission of the City of Palmdale, recommending approval of General Plan
  Amendment 23-001 and find that the project is consistent with Program Environmental
  Impact Report 22-002 prepared for the City’s General Plan.

  Senior Planner Magaña presented this item with an overview of the staff report and made
  herself available for questions.

  Chair Nemeth opened the public hearing on this item.

  Mr. Rick Norris spoke in opposition of the item and specifically asked for the density
  range of this site be reduced to 10 to 50 units per acre to accommodate housing for
  medical residents.

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing on this item.

  Vice Chair Henderson asked staff to explain 10 to 30 verses 10 to 50 related to density.

  Planning Manager Taggart clarified to Vice Chair Henderson that the density means that
  10 to 30 are the dwelling units are per acre or 10 to 50 dwelling units per acre.

  Senior Planner Magaña clarified that the request is to lower the maximum amount of
  dwelling units from 50 to 30.

  Commissioner Alvarez asked for clarification related to the restrictions requested for
  consideration or modification.

  Planning Manager Taggart clarified that the developer was requesting to lower the density
  from 30 to 50 to 10 to 50 dwelling units per acre within the Health and Wellness land use
  designation.

  Chair Nemeth reopened the public hearing item.
   Mr. McGaughey addressed the Commission and stated that for clarification purposes, his
  understanding of planned developments was for sites that were 20 acres or larger and
  advised that this site is 12 acres.

  Planning Manager Taggart answered Mr. McGaughey and stated that the new zoning
  code has made the requirements related to planned developments more flexible.

  Chair Nemeth stated that a planned development is flexible to accommodate proposed
  projects and does not change density requirements.

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing item.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-004; a Resolution of the Planning
  Commission of the City of Palmdale, recommending approval of General Plan
  Amendment 23-001 and find that the project is consistent with Program Environmental
  Impact Report 22-002 for the City’s General Plan.
  Moved by: Commissioner Fraga-Saenz and seconded by Commissioner Elize
  Motion passed with five Yes votes.

10.  PLANNING COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Planning Manager Taggart stated that the City is working on revising the Ordinance as it
  relates to mobile food vendors, which are currently allowed in 30 minute increments with
  property owner permissions and will be looking into how they can be regulated moving
  forward.

  Commissioner Alvarez stated that recent Assembly Bills help to align the ordinances to
  help regulate the food trucks.

  Chair Nemeth thanked Mr. Bettenhausen, Interim City Attorney and Mr. Justin Sauder,
  Associate Planner who will be moving on to other professional ventures.

  Chair Nemeth announced that applications to serve on the Planning Commission are still

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting to subdivide approximately five acres into three lots for the
purpose of constructing two restaurant buildings with drive-through facilities located at the
northwest corner of Rancho Vista Boulevard and Town Center Drive. There is currently
an assisted living facility onsite, which was previously approved through SPR 19-010 and
Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 19-009. As part of this application, the assisted living
facility and two restaurant buildings with drive through facilities will be contained on three
separate lots.

BACKGROUND

On June 16, 2005, the Planning Commission approved TPM 62432 and CUP 04-14
through Resolution No. PC-2005-028, with an expiration date of June 28, 2008. The
request was to subdivide five acres into five commercial lots for the purpose of
constructing a commercial shopping center in two phases totaling 39,950 square feet of
building area. A request for a two-year time extension, TPM 62432 Time Extension (TE)
and CUP 04-14 TE, was approved on June 5, 2008, through Resolution No. PC-2008-
033 with a new expiration date of June 28, 2010. The applicant was not able to record
the map prior to expiration nor was an application for a time extension submitted and the
TPM subsequentially expired. On October 10, 2019, the Planning Commission approved
SPR 19-010 and CUP 19-009, which was a request to construct a 42,000 square foot
assisted living facility on the southern portion of the site. The assisted living facility
included site grading, building construction, parking lot improvements, and landscaping
on the portion of the site containing the assisted living facility, and grading/erosion control
on the remaining vacant portion of the parcel. The project has completed construction
and is currently in operation.

Given that the previous TPM for the site expired, the applicant is requesting approval of
a new TPM through the submittal of TPM 83940 and SPR 22-017 for the subdivision of
the approximately five-acre parcel into three lots for the construction of the two drive-
through facilities. The request includes revisions to the project, which include a reduction
in number of lots and changes in lot sizes that result in two less lots than previously
approved.

The application was submitted on August 31, 2022, reviewed by staff, and deemed
incomplete on September 14, 2022, and then again on January 5, 2023. After resolution
of completeness items, the application was deemed complete on February 16, 2023, and
scheduled for the March 9, 2023, Planning Commission meeting.

Access/Circulation

The development proposes to utilize one existing driveway to Rancho Vista Boulevard,
which is the primary entrance to the existing assisted living facility. Internal circulation
will be provided through the parking area and drive aisles throughout the project site area.
The City Engineer and Los Angeles County Fire Department have reviewed the project
and determined that it is designed with adequate access to accommodate safe vehicular
flow.

Architecture

The proposed materials and colors comply with General Plan Land Use and Community
Design Element Policy LUD-4.6, which requires all facades of a building to be designed
with quality, care, and visual interest (four-sided architecture). The building elevations
have been designed to ensure consistency with the surrounding commercial buildings.
The colored elevations of the project indicate that the drive-through restaurant on Parcel 2
will consist of reveal panel siding with purple and varying shades of gray, weathered rustic
tile and tower elements provided at building entrances. The drive-through restaurant on
Parcel 3 will consist of stucco with varying shades of taupe and gray, reveal panel siding
with gray aluminum composite and dark bronze aluminum batten.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

On May 16, 2008, the Planning Commission adopted a MND and MMRP finding that the
project, with mitigation, would not have a significant impact on the environment. Given
the time that has elapsed, the applicant submitted updated studies for the project. In
addition, there are minor revisions to the project as previously proposed; however, the
revisions decrease the number of lots and development square footage, and therefore
decreases the impacts created by development. Staff has reviewed the revisions to the
project and has determined that a subsequent, supplement MND, or addendum as
described in California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Sections 15162,
15163, or 15164 is not required for the project because there are no significant revisions
to the project, there are no significant changes in circumstances and there is no new
information of substantial importance that will involve new significant environmental
effects or increase the severity of previously identified significant effects. Furthermore,
there are no new or additional significant impacts that were not already addressed by the
MND. As such, staff finds that the project is consistent with the previously adopted MND
and MMRP for TPM 62432 TE and CUP 04-14 TE.

OPTIONS

The Planning Commission has the following options:

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-006 approving TPM 83940 and SPR 22-017 and
  find that the project is consistent with the previously adopted MND and MMRP.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.
